title: Reset-arm rt_landlord_id guard pin is not unique — satisfied by the pre-existing consent-changed arm
evidence:
New guard added in both chains:
Makefile: `           'document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null' \`
Dockerfile: `    && grep -q -F 'document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null' server/priv/static/index.html \`

That exact substring already exists in the unchanged consent-changed reject arm of the OLD perl snippet (verified in the current Makefile, unchanged by this diff):
`opt_out_capturing();document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null`
detail: The pinned substring is already present in the pre-existing opt_out branch, so the guard passes even if the new reset-arm rt_landlord_id clear is reverted. It pins nothing the old snippet lacked — false regression protection on a load-bearing surface.
recommended_fix: Pin a substring unique to the reset arm, e.g. `rt_ph_reset=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=` (verified to occur exactly once), in both Makefile and Dockerfile guard lists.

title: OAuth path uses identify_with_set_once with an empty FirstTouch, contradicting that function's own 'prefer identify/3' guidance
evidence:
OAuth call (diff +):
`          posthog_client.identify_with_set_once(`
`            posthog,`
`            row.id,`
`            [#("email", json.string(row.email))],`
`            attribution.first_touch_set_once(attribution.FirstTouch(`
`              utm_source: "",`  ... all eight fields empty ...
`            )),`
`          )`

identify_with_set_once doc (server/src/posthog/posthog_client.gleam): "Pass `[]` for set_once_properties and prefer `identify/3` when there is nothing write-once to record."
detail: first_touch_set_once of an all-empty FirstTouch reduces to [] (it filters empties), so this is behaviorally identify/3. Routing an empty FirstTouch through the attribution masking/clamping function contradicts the documented API guidance and adds a meaningless object.
recommended_fix: Call posthog_client.identify(posthog, row.id, [#("email", json.string(row.email))]) directly, matching the documented preference and the email/password login path's shape.

title: complete_oauth_flow made pub for tests widens the in-process session-forgery boundary below the PKCE exchange
evidence:
New declaration (diff +):
`pub fn complete_oauth_flow(`
`  req: Request,`
`  db: pog.Connection,`
`  token_resp: types.OAuthTokenResponse,`
`  sentry: Sentry,`
`  secret_key: String,`
`  resend_api_key: String,`
`  posthog: PostHog,`
`) -> Response {`
Doc (diff +): "Public so integration tests can drive the funnel with a fabricated `OAuthTokenResponse` — the PKCE exchange above it needs a live Supabase."
detail: This function upserts a landlord and sets session cookies from token_resp with no validation that the token came from Supabase. Making it pub means any future server module could call it to forge a session, bypassing PKCE. Doc mitigates but does not enforce.
recommended_fix: Acceptable as-is given Gleam lacks test-only visibility and the server is monolithic. If tighter: keep private and expose a clearly-named `complete_oauth_flow_for_test`, or inject the token exchange as a parameter.
